angles.idea: Choose the priorities before the cleaning hours
angles.usefulInsight: The size of a home is only part of the booking decision: what is in the rooms and the depth of cleaning required also matter. Intended carousel story: open on the difficulty of choosing hours, explain why room count alone is incomplete, introduce a clearly labelled hypothetical distinction between priority jobs and jobs that can wait, and show how that distinction gives the hours discussion a clearer starting point. The reader learns to describe the clean they want rather than treat every room as an equal priority.

angles.idea: The first meeting is a choice, not a commitment
angles.usefulInsight: Meeting a proposed cleaner is not merely a handover of instructions: it is also a chance to decide whether you are comfortable with that person in your home. Intended static: a complete, reassuring observation that you can discuss the tasks and assess personal fit without having to accept the first cleaner introduced. The reader learns that their comfort is a legitimate part of the decision, alongside cleaning standards.

angles.usefulInsight: Arranging regular cleaning involves deciding how the cleaner will access the home, not necessarily keeping yourself available for every visit. Intended story: distinguish the initial conversation about tasks from ongoing access, explain the option for a vetted cleaner to hold keys and the Key Acknowledgement Form, then invite the reader to discuss access arrangements when enquiring. The reader learns that being present for every clean is not a service requirement.

blocks.text: Still have some questions about our house cleaning services? Here we have provided a list of the most frequently asked questions sent to our local offices
Simply leave your name and a form of contact, and we'll get back to you as soon as possible.
Frequently asked questions
How can we help?
If you don't find the question you're looking for, don't worry, just get in touch with us and we'll help you the best we can.
How many hours do I need?
It depends on the size of your home, how many rooms and how much is in them, plus the quality and depth of cleaning that you require.
Ultimately the choice is yours, and you may want fewer or more hours and then prioritise the rooms and jobs to be completed.
Below is a general guide for various property sizes:
How much will I pay?

Our hourly rates include the cleaner's wage and the agency fee. Rates vary depending on the area you're in and the number of hours you require each week. If you'd like a free quote, then contact us! All we require from you is the approximate number of hours you need and your postcode.
What time is your office open until?
The majority of our offices are open late and available at least 6 days of the week. Go to your local office to find out the opening times.
What sort of contract am I tied in to?

We don't believe in long and complicated contracts and do believe in being fair. Naturally, like any business, we have to have terms and conditions, and these can be found in the footer of any page. If you do ever need to cancel, all we ask is that you give us two month's notice or notice in accordance with the billing letter provided from your local office.
How do you vet the cleaners?

We first carry out a telephone interview. If the applicant seems suitable, we then arrange for a more thorough interview to take place in their own home. Only after taking proof of ID and address along with references do we accept them onto our database. We then monitor every cleaner thoroughly for the whole time they are with us.
Do I meet my cleaner before the first clean?

Of course! We know the cleaner will be in your home and that personalities are often as important as cleaning standards. Once we choose a cleaner for you, we'll arrange for them to come along and meet you so that you can approve our choice and discuss the cleaning tasks you require. It's important that your cleaner is someone you like so there's no need to agree to the first person we send you. Once you're satisfied that we've sent the right person for you, you can then mutually arrange a regular clean day and time. If you'd like to skip the interview and go straight to cleaning this can also be arranged.
What if my cleaner can't make it, or is sick?
Just give us a call, and we will provide you with a cleaner to cover.
Can I have an evening or weekend clean?

Yes of course! Our cleaners are fully flexible and will take on evening or weekend cleaning work. Please note in certain areas a supplement hourly charge may be added for cleans after 6pm or at weekends.
Can I have a clean once a month?
Most of our offices do not do monthly cleans - typically our most infrequent clean is every fortnight, or a one off.
Will I have to be at home when my cleaner visits?
No, our cleaners are vetted and are happy to hold your house keys. We will provide you with a Key Acknowledgement Form for your cleaner to sign.
Do I need to provide cleaning supplies and equipment?
Yes. Cleaners use the supplies and equipment already in the home. Most clients prefer to choose what is used. We ask that bleach is not used, for health and safety reasons.
Can I change my cleaner if I am not happy?
Yes, of course, we have a large and varied cleaner base, and we'd be happy to assign you someone different if you are unhappy for any reason. Just give us a call.
Do you have insurance cover?

Yes. Public liability insurance of at least £1,000,000 is in place, subject to our terms of business. The policy is indemnity cover, not new for old. Claims remain subject to liability being established and to the terms, conditions, exclusions and excesses of the policy. There is a £100 excess per claim. Where appropriate, customers should approach their household insurer first, as set out in our terms of business.
